content:
Burnley Borough Council has paid £3,364,836 to "POST OFFICE LTD - PAYOUT FUND" across 28 transactions since 2021/22, making it the council's 12th largest supplier by total spend. All payments are categorised under Chief Executive & Corporate, consistent with a benefits administration function. This investigation examines what the money is for, whether it represents value for money, and how Burnley compares to neighbouring councils.

INV-015: What Is the Post Office Payout Fund?

The Post Office Payout system is a mechanism by which councils can issue benefit payments — primarily Housing Benefit and Council Tax Support — to claimants who do not have bank accounts, or who prefer to collect cash at a Post Office counter. The council issues a payout voucher (via text, email, or letter), and the claimant redeems it at any Post Office branch. Post Office Ltd charges the council a transaction fee for each payout processed.

This is distinct from the standard BACS payment method used for the majority of Housing Benefit claimants. Post Office card accounts (POCAs) cannot receive BACS payments, so the Payout Fund serves as a cash-based alternative for claimants without mainstream banking.

The Spending Pattern

Our automated analysis flagged the Post Office Payout Fund for two reasons:

  • Round-number payments: 10 payments of exactly £100,000 were identified, accounting for £1,000,000 of the total. These are likely quarterly or periodic top-ups to a pre-funded payout account.
  • Near-duplicate detection: Payments of £100,000 on 5 June and 12 June 2023 (7 days apart), and £99,999 on 18 November and 24 November 2022, were flagged as near-duplicates.

The budget efficiency data shows £1,782,417 attributed to Post Office in the efficiency analysis — roughly half the total, suggesting the spending is split across financial years with the higher concentration in earlier years.

Cross-Council Comparison

We searched the spending data for all 15 Lancashire councils to benchmark Burnley's Post Office Payout spending:

Council Post Office Total Transactions Notes
Burnley£3,364,83628"POST OFFICE LTD - PAYOUT FUND"
Rossendale£1,299,95310"POST OFFICE LTD" (Customer Services)
PendleNot found-No Post Office payments in spending data
HyndburnNot found-No Post Office payments in spending data
LancasterNot found-No Post Office payments in spending data
ChorleyNot found-No Post Office payments in spending data
Preston, Fylde, Wyre, South RibbleNot found-No Post Office payments in spending data

This is a striking finding. Of the 10 Lancashire district councils checked, only Burnley and Rossendale show Post Office Payout payments in their transparency data. Burnley's spend is 2.6 times higher than Rossendale's. Either the other councils have moved entirely to BACS payments, or they categorise these payments differently in their spending data.

Burnley's population (~90,000) is roughly similar to Rossendale's (~70,000), yet Burnley pays 2.6x more — approximately £37 per head vs Rossendale's £19 per head over the same period.

The Universal Credit Impact

Housing Benefit is being progressively replaced by Universal Credit (UC), administered by the DWP rather than local councils. The UC migration accelerated from April 2024, with full-scale managed migration of remaining HB claimants underway. This has two implications:

  • Declining caseload: As HB claimants transfer to UC, the number of people needing Post Office payouts should be falling — the DWP pays UC directly, bypassing councils entirely.
  • Residual claimants: Those remaining on council-administered HB are typically pension-age claimants (exempt from UC migration), who are more likely to use Post Office cash collection.

The budget efficiency data suggests spending may be concentrating in earlier years (£1.78M in the efficiency analysis vs £3.36M total), consistent with a declining trend as UC migration reduces the caseload.

Other Post Office/Postal Spending

No additional Post Office payments beyond the Payout Fund were found in Burnley's spending data. No Royal Mail or other postage payments were identified in the top supplier statistics, though smaller postage costs may fall below the £500 transparency threshold.

Key Questions

  1. What percentage of Burnley's total Housing Benefit expenditure passes through the Post Office Payout Fund?
  2. How many individual claimants use this payment method, and has the number been declining with UC migration?
  3. What is the per-transaction fee charged by Post Office Ltd?
  4. Why do most Lancashire councils not show Post Office Payout payments — have they eliminated this method, or do they report it differently?
  5. Has the council considered incentivising claimants to switch to bank account payments to reduce costs?
  6. What is the year-by-year trend? Is spending declining as expected with UC migration?
  7. Are the near-duplicate payments (£100K within 7 days) legitimate pre-funding or processing errors?

Recommended FOI Request

A Freedom of Information request should seek: (1) the number of Housing Benefit claimants using Post Office Payout for each year since 2021; (2) the per-transaction fee payable to Post Office Ltd; (3) the total HB expenditure for each year, to calculate the percentage going through Post Office; (4) whether the council has a policy on transitioning claimants to BACS payments.

Investigation INV-015. All figures derived from publicly available spending data for Burnley and 9 other Lancashire district councils. Cross-council comparison conducted 10 April 2026.
